High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13806 of 2023
Applicant :- Anuj Gupta

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Gupta,Kaveri Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Ms. Kaveri Singh, learned counsels for the applicant and Sri Amit Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.0468 of 2023 registered under Sections 420, 504 and 506 IPC at Police Station- Modi Nagar,
District Ghaziabad with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have sold the house of the informant for a consideration of Rs.18,30,000/- and had categorically informed the informant that there was no Anuj Gupta vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196617791/
1 loan on it.

entities.text: Anuj Gupta vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But later on, it came to the knowledge of the informant, as a recovery certificate was issued regarding the said house, that the applicant had appeared as a guarantor in the said loan taken by the co-accused person Arvind Gupta.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by about seven years and there is no explanation of the said delay cased.
The said allegations are false.
The case of civil nature has been converted into criminal one.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
(v). that the applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness;

entities.text: Anuj Gupta vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
